title: xi ability recipe
description: What `xi ability compose` reads and the model viewer's Ability Mixer writes: lanes of retail sources plus the commands of the new `main` routine at absolute frames. See docs/ability/mixer.md.

dir.description: 4-char name of the effect directory written around the sections (default: the first four alphanumerics of name, padded with _). A job ability or spell is that one directory; for a per-race (weapon-skill) build it is the effect folder inside the race root <tag>_<c> (hf_1: the race's tag, then this name's first character), beside a clip folder of the root's name holding the clips and weapon traces.

target.description: How the recipe is meant to be published. `xi dats` records the numbers it allocated here on the published copy.

total.description: The routine's totalDelay (its end). A recipe from `xi ability recipe` carries the source's own so the header round-trips; otherwise the routine ends where its last window does: start + dur, or start + dur × loops for a clip that plays N times.

sources.description: One lane per key (motion / vfx / sound are the mixer's; any name works). A `ws:N` spec without a race is race-bound: the recipe composes once per race.

routine.description: Routine tag the lane's events are read from. null: the DAT is a bare clip pack (Basic, the emotes) with no routine; its events are PlayClip commands built from the template.

name.description: Display name (the mixer keeps the catalog entry's).

events.description: One command each in the new `main` routine, in any order (sorted by start, then `order`).

generators.description: In-place edits to a lane's particle generators (0x05 sections). Compose writes them to the lane's copy of the section before it goes into the output, on every race's copy for a race-bound lane; the source DAT is never touched. One entry per lane + ref. An entry whose generator no event fires is unused; one whose generator is not in the lane's DAT is an error.

ref.description: The generator's name as the source DAT has it. A rename compose makes to settle a name collision does not change it.

curves.description: New keys for a lane's keyframe curves (0x19 ParticleKeyFrameData sections). A curve is shared: every generator of the lane that names it plays the new keys. One entry per lane + ref.

ref.description: The curve's name as the source DAT has it.

keys.description: [time, value] pairs, as many as the source curve has (the section cannot grow). `time` is a fraction of the particle's life; the last key keeps the source's time (1, which ends the curve) whatever is written here, and no earlier key may have time 1.

textures.description: PNGs that replace a lane's textures (0x20 sections). Compose encodes each as DXT3 (each side the nearest power of two from 4 to 256, alpha halved) and keeps the section's id, 16-character name and flags, so every mesh and sprite sheet of that lane that names the texture draws it, on every race's copy. An entry is one 0x20 section: the one with that `ref` and `name`, or without `name` the first with that `ref`. One entry per lane + ref + name (no name counts as a value of its own); two entries on one section are an error at compose. An entry whose texture nothing the mix fires draws is unused (the report says so); one whose texture is not in the lane's DAT is an error. When another lane already puts a different texture of that name in the output, this lane's is renamed (and its meshes patched), and the report gives the name it went out under.

ref.description: The texture's 4-character section id as the source DAT has it (its 16-character name goes in `name`).

name.description: The texture's 16-character name as the source DAT stores it, to tell apart textures that share `ref`: ROM/11/21 gives five textures the id `faid` ("faida01 faida01" to "faida01 faida05"), and a name is never repeated. Without it the entry is the first texture of `ref`, as a recipe written before names were.

spec.description: Anything `xi ability inspect` accepts: ja:N, spell:N, ws:N[:Race], fid:N, ROM/x/y, or a path.

datId.description: 4-char section id the command names (clip `b00?` with the client's `?` wildcard, generator `g004`, sound pointer `8050`, routine `mdam`): 1–4 printable ASCII characters, not only spaces.

sectionId.description: A section's name: 1–4 printable ASCII characters. Trailing padding is ignored.

textureName.description: A texture's 16-character name as a 0x20 section stores it at +0x11 (an 8-character namespace and a localName, "carel3  ho"): 1–16 printable ASCII characters, not only spaces. Compared with trailing spaces and NULs dropped, as a mesh's binding compares it.

edit.description: One same-size, little-endian write inside a generator, addressed by where the bytes sit in the format (never by file offset, so it holds on every race's copy). Values are absolute: applying an edit twice changes nothing. The 16-byte section header, the stream-offset table at +0x80..0x8F and an op's config dword are never writable. Layouts: docs/fx/effects.md, docs/ability/mixer.md.

sec.description: 0 = the generator header; 1–4 = an op stream (1 generator updaters, 2 initializers, 3 updaters, 4 expiration handlers).

op.description: sec 1–4: the opcode to write into, found by walking the stream (config dword: op = & 0xFF, size in dwords = (>> 8) & 0x1F, op 0 ends the stream). Left out when sec is 0.

nth.description: Which occurrence of that opcode in the stream, from 0.

at.description: Byte offset of the write. sec 0: from the section start (the spawn interval is at 118 = 0x76), 16 <= at and at + size <= 128. sec 1–4: from the op's config dword, 4 <= at and at + size <= the op's own size.

type.description: `datid` writes a 4-character section id, padded the way the DAT pads it; the section (a texture, mesh, sprite sheet, curve or sound pointer) must be in the lane's DAT, and compose carries it and what it names.

value.description: One value, or a list of consecutive ones (an RGBA colour is four `u8`, a scale three `f32`).

mask.description: Integer types only: just these bits are written, the rest stay as the source has them (a flag in a bitfield). Must fit the type.

png.description: The PNG, alpha at full scale (255 = opaque, as the model viewer shows textures). The validator also decodes a data URI: at most 2 MiB, a PNG signature, and an IHDR with each side 1–4096.

oneOf.description: The file's bytes as a data URI, standard padded base64 (what the model viewer writes).
A path relative to the recipe file's folder, inside it. load_recipe reads the file and puts its data URI in its place; `dats prepare` stores that self-contained recipe.

from.description: Lane (a key of `sources`) the command and its sections come from. Left out, the event is a command of no lane — a lock, a hit, a link to a shared (ROM/0/0.DAT) or actor routine added by hand — which carries its own `raw` bytes: compose writes them as given (delay, `dur` and a named routine's `ref` stamped in), gathers nothing for them and renames nothing in them, and every race's DAT has them. Such a command cannot be a generator, sound, clip or weapon trace (0x02 0x1E 0x2D 0x3F, 0x0A 0x0B 0x4A 0x53 0x60, 0x05, 0x2C): those name a section of their lane's DAT. A link to a routine of a lane's own DAT keeps that lane, so compose carries the routine.

op.description: Routine opcode (docs/fx/effect_system.md §3): 0x05 clip, 0x02 generator, 0x0A/0x0B sound, 0x03 link, 0x2C trace, 0x1E dampen…

start.description: Absolute frame (60/s routine ticks). The writer turns it back into the format's relative delays.

dur.description: The command's duration field (emit window, lock length, clip window).

order.description: Tie-break for events on the same start frame.

loops.description: Clip (0x05) only: 0 = loop forever, N = play N times then hold.

raw.description: Exact command bytes (from `inspect --json`, or built by the model viewer for a command of no lane). Wins over routine/offset and op/ref lookup. The validator also reads them as the client walks a routine: whole dwords, 8 bytes at least, as many as the size in byte +1 says (low 5 bits, in dwords), and byte 0 the event's `op`. A command that names a routine, sound or generator (the links 0x03 0x09 0x3B 0x3C 0x57, 0x30, 0x5F, 0x73, 0x85; the sounds; the generators) is 16 bytes at least with 0 at +0xC, where the client keeps a pointer once it has looked the name up, and without a `ref` its name at +8 is 1–4 printable ASCII characters, padded with NULs.

routine.description: With `offset`: the source routine the command is copied from.

offset.description: With `routine`: byte offset of the command inside that routine's sec2.

name.description: Display label (the mixer keeps the inspector's command name, e.g. PlayClip). Compose ignores it.

row.description: Mixer layout only: which row of its track the event's pill sits in (0 = the top row). Compose ignores it; timing comes from `start` alone.

examples.name: blue_fire
examples.description: Fire's flame recoloured and widened: generator g000's tint, scale and spawn interval, and the curve its height follows.

examples.name: golden_cure
examples.description: Cure III's glow drawn with a small gold dot: texture `ho` ("carel3  ho"), which the `ho` mesh of ho00 and the `hp` mesh of sh01 both name.

examples.name: fast_blade_by_hand
examples.description: Fast Blade's swings, trace, hit sparks and sounds from its own DAT, and the locks, activation flash, hit and added effect retail puts around them added by hand: commands of no lane, each its own bytes. The local hit1 / hit2 links keep their lane, so compose carries those routines.
